8.t: The Oliver band in San Francisco and Minor Hall's firing
8.s: Playing at a dance hall on Walker Street in San Francisco with Oliver; lineup and Oliver firing drummer Minor Hall and violinist Jimmy Palao without notice.
8.ch: Chicago and Oliver's band in California
8.q: Oh yeah. See, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that was over in Frisco and I was playing over to the Picola Dance Hall on Walker Street.

8.t: First trip west and King Oliver's Nine Kings in San Francisco
8.s: Garland first came west in 1917, then returned in 1920 with King Oliver's band, with the lineup he lists, playing a dance hall in San Francisco and then Oakland.
8.q: And when did you first come out the West Coast? Well, it's like I told you, the first time I come to the West Coast, when I was in Tennessee 10 in 17. 1917.

8.t: The 1921 King Oliver band on the West Coast
8.s: Garland lists the personnel of Oliver's 1921 band, which played nightclubs and shows from arrangements.
8.q: : No, Dave -- Dave -- Dave -- played a mellophone and alto saxophone. Jimmy Palao played tenor saxophone and violin.

8.t: The Plantation club and Oliver's big band
8.s: He describes the Plantation and Oliver's dozen-piece band stranded for payment.
8.q: Over there, because that's where I was going. Nowhere was here, I was always over there. Over there in Oakland. He went to work. He went to work. And he goes to work at where this place was at 35th and Calumet. Oh yeah. Where Al-Twenty's old place was. That's where they built the cage. The cage?…

8.t: Leaving Dreamland for San Francisco in 1921
8.s: Oliver went to the Royal Garden, then the band moved to the Pecola dance hall in San Francisco, leaving Chicago May 30, 1921.
8.q: Oh, no. Joe went over to Royal Garden and I was at the Dreamland. Then Joe left and come join us at there. Then I turned the band over to Joe. See? At the Dreamland. Then we left the Dreamland to come to the Pecola Dance Hall on Market Street.

768.t: Band breaks up; joining Oliver at Dreamland
768.s: The band broke up at Dreamland; she stayed as house pianist, then worked with Oliver when he came to Dreamland, and they got an offer for San Francisco.
768.q: Oh, well, Eddie Garland, oh yeah, Eddie Garland, the boys, oh, Dewey went back to New Orleans. And anyway, the band broke up while we were at Dreamland. I don't know for what reason. The band broke up, but I stayed on as a pianist and every band came, I worked with them. So, a clarinet player, a…

768.t: San Francisco, Oakland and the Bertha Gonsoulin question
768.s: They worked at the Pergola Ballroom in San Francisco for six months, then Oakland; she clarifies that Bertha Gonsoulin replaced her but made no records, and she returned to Chicago in early 1922.
768.q: No, no. We went to this ballroom in San Francisco and stayed six months. Then, we went across to Oakland and played at the cabaret for about two or three weeks. I don't remember the cabaret, but it was in Oakland. Then, after that, after that job closed, they decided to go to Los Angeles. Well, I…

11.t: King Oliver's band in San Francisco and Clem's Balcony Ballroom band
11.s: Hearing Oliver's band on Market Street, Clem's own travelling work and eleven-piece band, and the tune King Porter Stomp.
11.q: I'd go all over. I always had a car and that's how I used to make my living. I'd go up this far to Portland, Oregon. Just play around, play around and come back down. Then for about nine months, I worked on Market Street. I don't remember the years. It was the Balcony Ballroom when I had 11 pieces…

11.t: Barbary Coast sextet, living in Oakland, Orie Nelson and Wade Whaley
11.s: Eight months with Sid before Slocum replaced him, moving to Oakland about 1922, and Mutt Carey and Ory at the Creole Cafe.
11.ch: Oakland and the Bay Area scene
11.q: No, I've been up here since about twenty-two, yeah about nineteen-twenty-two. But I would go back and forth, I just didn't... You had about thirty-six years. Uh huh.

291.t: Leaving Celestin's Tuxedo band when King Oliver wrote
291.s: He told Celestin he was leaving; Oliver wrote through Manuel Perez after hearing My Josephine.
291.q: I just told him I was going to go, and he was glad for me. He hated to lose me, but he thought it was a good opportunity for me.

291.t: 'My Josephine' and the call from King Oliver
291.s: His composition 'My Josephine' made Celestin's band a hit, the record reached Chicago, and Oliver sent for him. He left in 1927 to join Oliver in St. Louis.
291.q: Jeanette Sullivan. So we got her to play in the band. And the band made a great success. The band then, I composed a number and we called it My Josephie. And the number made such a hit with the people that it actually swarmed Ridgely's Tuxedo. Really? By the way Ridgely called his band Ridgely's…

641.s: Joe says Ory told him he fired Oliver and replaced him with Mutt, and that Joe left Los Angeles on an ocean liner before Ory returned.
641.ch: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
641.q: Oh, yeah. Papa Mutt and Ory had worked off and on all their life, I guess. Ory said when he fired Joe Oliver... Oliver used to play with Ory's band, and Ory said he fired him and Papa Mutt took his place.

641.t: Joe Oliver's 1921 trip to California and Ram Hall
641.s: Joe recalls Ram Hall and Tudie coming west with Oliver in 1921 and a photo of Ory and Tudie on the San Francisco dock.
641.ch: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
641.q: Well, like I said, Ram first came here I know in 1921 with Joe Oliver. And I seen a picture (I don't know how I got that picture, if somebody gave it to me) of Kid Ory and Tudie standing on the dock in San Francisco...

904.t: King Oliver hears My Josephine and Paul leaves for St. Louis
904.s: Oliver tracks Paul down through Manuel Perez; Paul leaves with Willie Foster and Red Allen to meet Oliver in St. Louis.
904.q: So, in the, up until, I went back with Solis there, last of 25 and I stayed until 27. And by that time King Oliver had heard that record, My Josephine and hearing all the work on the saxophone. And right down to Manuel Perez and found who it was and Manuel told him who it was. And in through…

184.t: San Francisco with Oliver and the dispute that ended it
184.s: The band went to San Francisco with Davey Jones added; Hall refused to lay off Jimmy Palao, Oliver dismissed him, the union ruled in his favour, and he returned to Chicago to work with Jimmy Noone.
184.q: So some man up there, I forget his name, he wanted a Dixland band to work at a place called Pekrola Dance Hall on Market Street. I have a picture of that. Yeah, so he got in touch with these guys, so we had to add another man to the band to make eight pieces. So he picked up a fellow by the name of…

263.t: Natty Dominique, Kid Ory's band in San Francisco, and Ory's leadership
263.s: He recalls Natty Dominique sitting in at Chicago's Beehive, then joining Kid Ory in 1953 at the Hangover Club in San Francisco and describes Ory's leadership and the band's players.
263.q: I think that was only for a couple of months. Remember once Dr. Bichet, his brother, Sidney's brother, the trombonist, came up. Were you there when he sat in one night? No, I wasn't. Might have been a different engagement or something. I think I even have a photograph. I don't remember if you were…

151.t: Nighthawks club in New Orleans, rejoining and leaving King Oliver
151.s: Back in New Orleans Reason leads a Fats Waller-style small band, then returns to a ragged Oliver band in Savannah and slips away after a Vicksburg dance.
151.ch: Early years with Paul Barnes and King Oliver
151.q: And the nighthawks on Roman and Kodai. And the club owner's name was Peter Tato, a tagging fella. And he had a color fella, was the manager named Peter Robinson from Mississippi. And I sat in with the band. During that time, Fetch Wilder's style was very popular. And I used to sing and play like…
